exposure_qualifications: A vulnerable locked dependency version is established; an exposed production endpoint is NOT established and is not claimed here.

Both next.config.ts files set output: "export" and images: { unoptimized: true }, and the comments describe GitHub Pages static hosting plus a Tauri tauri:// local webview. That is static configuration evidence only; it does not by itself prove that no Node-served Next runtime exists anywhere (previews, ad-hoc hosts, contributor machines), and hosting/OS/container-image/runtime reachability were explicitly not audited.

Static config also does not prove dev/test-time safety: site-e2e.yml and the SPARQ_VR screenshot suite (scripts/vr.sh) run `next dev`, a real server process that is in the alerted version range. Whether the dev server exposes an image-optimization route despite images.unoptimized, and whether it is bound beyond localhost in CI, was not verified.

GHSA-2xp9-vwfh-vxw4 depends on the sharp/libheif AVIF path. sharp appears only as an optionalDependency of next (^0.34.3) in the supplied lock excerpt; whether sharp is actually installed in the resolved tree, on which platforms, and whether any AVIF input reaches it, were not verified.

GHSA-p293-qw3h-jr36 is conditioned by the publisher on Windows-filesystem hosting. No Windows host was confirmed and none was excluded — CI runner OS and contributor developer OS were not audited. A contributor running `next dev` on Windows is a plausible in-scope configuration that the static export posture does not cover.
"Critical" is the publisher's general-case severity for the package, not a repository-specific exposure rating for sparq; nothing in this review upgrades or downgrades that label.
The favourable-looking export/unoptimized posture is a reason to treat this as routine rather than incident-grade — it is not a reason to close, dismiss, or indefinitely defer the alerts.
patch_validation_requirements: Re-scan the full lockfile for every `node_modules/**/next` entry (and any vendored/nested copy) to confirm the single 15.5.21 instance is the only alerted artifact before and after the bump.
Post-bump `npm ls next` must report 15.5.24 resolved for both `site` and `gui/app`; no residual 15.5.x < 15.5.24 anywhere in the tree.

Lock diff must be bounded: next, @next/env, the @next/swc-* optional platform set, and only such sharp/transitive churn as npm mechanically re-resolves. Any unrelated dependency drift is a signal to redo the bump with a targeted install rather than a full re-resolve.
Confirm `npm ci` reproducibility from the amended lock and that integrity hashes are registry-sourced for 15.5.24.

Diff must show zero change to site/next.config.ts and gui/app/next.config.ts: output "export", images.unoptimized, the NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_PATH switch and its legacy fallbacks, trailingSlash, experimental.optimizePackageImports ["radix-ui"], the SPARQ_VR devIndicators gate, and both webpack extensionAlias/@sparq/client aliases preserved verbatim.
Confirm 15.5.24's published `engines` still satisfies the repo's Node baseline (15.5.21 declares ^18.18.0 || ^19.8.0 || >= 20.0.0) and that its React/react-dom peer ranges still admit ^19.0.0.

CI must pass on the protected pipeline: site-e2e.yml (next dev based), both static export builds (build:web and the Tauri beforeBuildCommand build:tauri path), and lint. Treat the VR/screenshot suite as the highest-sensitivity check — a Next patch can shift dev-overlay/indicator rendering and move baselines; any baseline delta must be explained, not silently re-recorded.
Verify the exported out/ trees are unchanged in shape (root-relative when NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_PATH='', /sparq and /app fallbacks intact) so the Pages and Tauri consumers are unaffected.
Confirm no repository protection is bypassed: change lands via a PR through protected CI, not a direct push, and not via an admin override.

Close-out condition: alerts 106 and 107 must auto-resolve on merge because the patched version is installed. No manual dismissal is authorized. Re-check the alert list after merge to confirm both closed and that no superseding Next advisory has been published in the interim.
Record in the follow-up whether the declared floors were left at ^15.5.21 or raised to ^15.5.24, so a future clean re-resolve is not silently able to drop back below the patch.
blockers: Single implementation lane: PR 6478 (engine) currently occupies protected CI and there is no second lane. Opening a competing Next-bump PR now conflicts with the stated lane constraint and with restrained model spend — file the tracking follow-up now, execute the bump when the lane frees or as an explicitly agreed low-cost interrupt.

Unverified inputs that gate any exposure statement: sharp presence in the resolved tree, CI runner and contributor host OS, full contents of site-e2e.yml, and whether any Node-served Next deployment exists outside the described static/Tauri targets.
This review authorizes no code change, install, build, exploit reproduction, deployment, or alert dismissal — the bump and its validation are a separate authorized action.

limitations: Evidence-only assessment with no tool use: the supplied lockfile excerpt, workspace manifests, next.config.ts contents, advisory text and search counts were taken as given and not independently re-fetched or re-verified.
